summary: Edward Upham worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He was a member of the Royal Asiatic Society from circa 1824 to 1834 and a fellow of the Society of Antiquaries of London.

Edward Vernon Arnold specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Edward Byles Cowell at Cambridge (B.A., Litt.D.) and under Rudolf von Roth at Tübingen. Arnold was a fellow at Trinity College, Cambridge, and served as professor at Bangor University (1884–1924).

Edward W. Said studied at St. George's School, Victoria College, Northfield Mount Hermon School, Princeton University, and Harvard University. He was a professor of English and Comparative Literature at Columbia University from circa 1963 to 2003.

Edward Washburn Hopkins studied at Columbia and under Albrecht Weber and Ernst Windisch at Leipzig (Ph.D.). He held posts at Columbia, Bryn Mawr College (1885–1895), and Yale University (1895–1926) in the fields of Indology and linguistics.
Edward William West worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at King's College London (1839–1842) and under Duncan Forbes (circa 1842–1844) and Martin Haug (1867–1873).

Edward Winslow Bastian worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He was a research scholar at Banaras Hindu University and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, also studying under Geshe Lobsang, Geshe Lobsang Donyo, and Lobsang Tenzin.

Edward Winter Clark studied linguistics at Brown University (M.A.), Newton Theological Institution, and Colgate Rochester Crozer Divinity School. He served as a missionary for the American Baptist Missionary Union from 1869 to 1911.

Edwin Abbott Abbott studied at the City of London School and St John's College. He held teaching posts at St John's College, King Edward's School, Birmingham, Clifton College, and the City of London School (1865–1889).

Edwin Arnold studied at King's College London and Oxford. Active in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Japanology, he was Principal of Deccan College (1856–1861), taught at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and lectured at Keio University.

Edwin Capers Kirkland worked in Indology and other fields. He earned his Ph.D. at Northwestern University, taught at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (circa 1934–1946), and was Professor of English at the University of Florida starting in 1946.

Edwin Felix Thomas Atkinson, educated at Trinity College Dublin, worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as President of The Asiatic Society (1886–1887) and Accountant General for the Government of Bengal (circa 1888–1890).

Edwin Francis Bryant works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He completed his doctorate at Columbia University (circa 1991–1997), taught at Harvard University (circa 1998–2002), and became Associate Professor of Hinduism at Rutgers University circa 2003.

Edwin Gerow studied Indology and philosophy under J. A. B. van Buitenen, Louis Renou, George V. Bobrinskoy, and V. Ranganathan. He held posts at the University of Washington (circa 1965–1985) and Reed College (circa 1985–1996).

Edwin Greaves studied at Western College (circa 1876–1880). In Indology and linguistics, he was a London Missionary Society missionary (circa 1881–1920) and served as Principal of the London Missionary Society's College, Benares, and the Missionary Language School, Lucknow.

Edwin Hotchkiss Tuttle studied at Yale University from circa 1897 to 1901. Working in linguistics and Indology, he held posts as a language teacher at the Mackenzie School and the Boys' Latin School of Maryland.

Edwin Lee Johnson studied linguistics and Indology at the University of Mississippi and Vanderbilt University (Ph.D.). He taught at Quitman College, Alexander Institute, and Vanderbilt University, where he became Professor of Latin and Greek in 1935.
Edwin Möhrke, an Indologist, studied philology at the University of Marburg in 1923 and completed his Ph.D. under Helmuth von Glasenapp at the University of Königsberg in 1934.

Edwin Norris worked in linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He held posts at the East India Company, the Foreign Office (1847–1866), and the Royal Asiatic Society (1837–1861), where he served as Assistant Secretary and editor of its journal.

Edwin Whitfield Fay studied at Rhodes College, Johns Hopkins (Ph.D.), and Leipzig under Karl Brugmann and Ernst Windisch. A scholar of linguistics and Indology, he held posts at Michigan, Washington and Lee, and the University of Texas at Austin.

Egaku Maeda studied Buddhist studies and Indology at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji, Shoson Miyamoto, Hajime Nakamura, and Kogen Mizuno. He held professorships at Tokai Gakuen, Meijo University, and Aichi Gakuin University (1972–2002).
